items.english: "He's not so flippant as all that, Kume as an author, eh," said the knowledge-face fellow.
"You can tell that from his work up till now, can't you?" That was the near-sighted man.
"If he's a flippant man, it's only natural he makes flippant work. Whether to like it or dislike it is left to the reader's side."
notes: No speaker named in the text; taken as the host, as p108 has Nekohachi receive it as the host's argument.

items.english: "So it's up to the customer, is it, eh," Nekohachi took the host's argument this way. And growing eager to cozy up to it, "But he's a man with a deal of teasing wit in him, and I think him a great man, eh?"
notes: Tea-wit for 茶気, his performer’s word for love of a droll trick; kept as teasing rather than ennobled.

items.english: "Wa-ha, ha," two or three of them raised their voices together.

"Sensei," the student-like fellow who had not said a word till now spoke for the first time, his words carrying that nervous tone. "I've not read a thing of Mr Kume's, so I've no right to say anything about the man, but it seems to me a piece of fiction has no depth unless the author's personality is backing it, eh?"
notes: Sensei kept; addressed to the room, presumably the host. Personality backing for 人物が裏づけ.

items.english: "You always talk like an idealist, but even the realists on the other side would never deny that."
"Then I feel easy about that, but..."
"Only we don't come to a stop at the sort of thing you mean."
"That's just what I can't..." the other said, cocking his head a little to one side.
"Even if the man's character comes out, unless a life of that character comes out with it, it still won't be concrete, will it?"
notes: Character for 人格 and concrete for ぐたい的, keeping the group's borrowed abstraction flat against Nekohachi's patter.

items.english: "..." The nervous student smiled now and made his bow. "Then even I can understand that."

data.say: Drafted p105-p117 keeping the literati flat and Nekohachi wheedling, with one speaker inferred.
